fix(provider-utils): ignore inherited media type signature tables (#24488)

## Background

`detectMediaType` documents that unsupported top-level segments return
`undefined`. Names inherited from `Object.prototype` instead resolve to
functions or objects, then throw `TypeError: signatures is not
iterable`.

Found through source review, not production use. This is a small
robustness correction to the exported utility; no built-in provider flow
passing these names or security impact is claimed.

## Summary

- Reject inherited signature-table properties with an own-property
check.
- Add regression cases for `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, and
`hasOwnProperty`.
- Add a patch changeset.

Validation: all 81 tests in `detect-media-type.test.ts` pass in Node
with Vitest 4.1.11. Removing the guard causes exactly the four new cases
to fail (77 pass). Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Guideline
discovery found no applicable guidelines.

Full workspace installation exhausted local disk capacity. A separate
minimal Vitest installation was used for the focused test suite. Full
workspace type checking was attempted and stopped after missing
dependency/configuration errors from the incomplete workspace install.
Edge tests could not start because `@edge-runtime/vm` was unavailable.
Repository CI still needs to validate the complete workspace.

## End-to-End Verification

Built-package verification is blocked locally: the workspace dependency
installation ran out of disk space. No live provider or application flow
was exercised; this change concerns the directly exported utility. The
source-level reproduction below exercises the actual local utility and
uint8 dependency, using Node 24.13.0 to strip TypeScript. It does not
substitute a published package. This is source-level verification, not a
completed built-package end-to-end run.

Save outside the checkout as `/tmp/ai-media-type.mjs`:

```js
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { stripTypeScriptTypes } from 'node:module';

const root = `${process.cwd()}/packages/provider-utils/src/`;
const asModule = source => 'data:text/javascript;base64,' +
  Buffer.from(stripTypeScriptTypes(source)).toString('base64');
const utils = asModule(readFileSync(root + 'uint8-utils.ts', 'utf8'));
const source = readFileSync(root + 'detect-media-type.ts', 'utf8')
  .replace("'./uint8-utils'", JSON.stringify(utils));
const { detectMediaType } = await import(asModule(source));
for (const topLevelType of ['image', 'text', 'constructor', '__proto__', 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty']) {
  try {
    console.log(topLevelType, '=>', detectMediaType({
      data: new Uint8Array([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47]), topLevelType,
    }));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(topLevelType, '=>', String(error));
  }
}
```

From the checkout root, run `node /tmp/ai-media-type.mjs` before and
after the guard. Before: all four inherited names throw `TypeError:
signatures is not iterable`. After: all return `undefined`. In both
runs, `image` returns `image/png` and `text` returns `undefined`. The
reproduction requires Node 24 and no provider credentials.

fix(anthropic): restrict MCP tools during JSON output fallback (#24697)

## Background

Structured output can fall back to an internal JSON response tool, which
widens the provider's tool choice to `any`. MCP connectors retained
their original configuration even when the caller selected `none` or a
named application tool. A named choice that falls back to `auto` because
of model or thinking restrictions had the same gap without structured
output.

## Summary

Disable MCP connector tools before sending JSON-tool fallback requests
with a restricted caller tool choice, and named-tool requests that fall
back to `auto`. Preserve connector allowlists and leave their
configuration unchanged for unrestricted choices. Generation and
streaming share the fix and the existing inline-tool fallback
restriction condition. Retaining server descriptors preserves names
referenced by MCP conversation history; only tool execution is disabled.

Add regression coverage for automatic fallback with open-object schemas,
explicit JSON-tool mode, both restricted choices, and unrestricted
choices across default, enabled, disabled, and allowlisted MCP servers.
Also cover named-choice fallbacks and preservation of MCP configuration
when native tool choices remain enforced. No public API changes.

## End-to-End Verification

A local request-capture script exercises the exported Anthropic
provider's generation and streaming methods before and after rebuilding
the checkout. It captures outgoing requests and returns synthetic
JSON/SSE responses; live Anthropic/MCP end-to-end verification remains
unavailable.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction code, setup, and before/after results</summary>

Prerequisites: supported Node.js, pnpm 12, installed locked workspace
dependencies. No API credentials are needed for this local check. The
script uses a custom fetch implementation and an inert `.invalid`
connector URL, so it sends no external requests. Save the following
script outside the checkout as
`/tmp/ai-sdk-mcp-choice/request-check.mjs`:

```js
import { createAnthropic } from '@ai-sdk/anthropic';

console.log('local package:', import.meta.resolve('@ai-sdk/anthropic'));
const provider = createAnthropic({
  apiKey: 'local-request-check',
  fetch: async (_url, init) => {
    const body = JSON.parse(init.body);
    console.log(JSON.stringify({
      stream: body.stream === true,
      tools: body.tools.map(tool => tool.name),
      toolChoice: body.tool_choice,
      mcpServers: body.mcp_servers,
    }));
    const usesJsonTool = body.tools.some(tool => tool.name === 'json');
    const message = {
      id: 'msg_local', type: 'message', role: 'assistant',
      model: body.model,
      content: usesJsonTool
        ? [{ type: 'tool_use', id: 'call_json', name: 'json', input: { greeting: 'hello' } }]
        : [{ type: 'text', text: 'hello' }],
      stop_reason: 'tool_use', stop_sequence: null,
      usage: { input_tokens: 1, output_tokens: 1 },
    };
    if (!body.stream) return Response.json(message);
    const events = [
      { type: 'message_start', message: { ...message, content: [], stop_reason: null } },
      { type: 'content_block_start', index: 0, content_block: { type: 'tool_use', id: 'call_json', name: 'json', input: {} } },
      { type: 'content_block_delta', index: 0, delta: { type: 'input_json_delta', partial_json: '{"greeting":"hello"}' } },
      { type: 'content_block_stop', index: 0 },
      { type: 'message_delta', delta: { stop_reason: 'tool_use', stop_sequence: null }, usage: { output_tokens: 1 } },
      { type: 'message_stop' },
    ];
    if (!usesJsonTool) events.splice(1, 3,
      { type: 'content_block_start', index: 0, content_block: { type: 'text', text: '' } },
      { type: 'content_block_delta', index: 0, delta: { type: 'text_delta', text: 'hello' } },
      { type: 'content_block_stop', index: 0 },
    );
    return new Response(events.map(event => `event: ${event.type}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`).join(''), {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' },
    });
  },
});
for (const method of ['doGenerate', 'doStream']) {
  for (const toolChoice of [{ type: 'none' }, { type: 'tool', toolName: 'greeting' }]) {
    console.log(method, toolChoice);
    const result = await provider('claude-sonnet-4-5')[method]({
      prompt: [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Return a short greeting.' }] }],
      responseFormat: { type: 'json', schema: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true } },
      tools: [{ type: 'function', name: 'greeting', inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} } }],
      toolChoice,
      providerOptions: { anthropic: {
        mcpServers: [{ type: 'url', name: 'inert', url: 'https://connector.invalid/mcp' }],
      } },
    });
    if (method === 'doStream') for await (const part of result.stream) {
      if (part.type === 'error') throw part.error;
    }
  }
}

for (const method of ['doGenerate', 'doStream']) {
  for (const [modelId, thinking] of [
    ['claude-opus-5-5', undefined],
    ['claude-sonnet-4-5', { type: 'enabled', budgetTokens: 1024 }],
  ]) {
    console.log(method, 'named choice without JSON fallback', modelId);
    const result = await provider(modelId)[method]({
      prompt: [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Return a short greeting.' }] }],
      tools: [{ type: 'function', name: 'greeting', inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} } }],
      toolChoice: { type: 'tool', toolName: 'greeting' },
      providerOptions: { anthropic: {
        thinking,
        mcpServers: [{ type: 'url', name: 'inert', url: 'https://connector.invalid/mcp' }],
      } },
    });
    if (method === 'doStream') for await (const part of result.stream) {
      if (part.type === 'error') throw part.error;
    }
  }
}
```

For each before/after checkout, install dependencies, build its local
package and run the same script from the workspace-linked example:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/anthropic...
cd examples/ai-functions
node --input-type=module < /tmp/ai-sdk-mcp-choice/request-check.mjs
```

Initial baseline: `a6860a687011dbf025388ee419db730e05fb9ce0`. The
original four JSON-tool cases were run before and after the initial fix.
The script was then extended with four named-choice fallback cases and
run unchanged before and after the review correction, using
`8cbb9cbb62358eaceeac79837171d72505583d33` as that baseline. The final
fixed revision is `00371ee04b2724ef67efc7fefb12578775370cdb`. Both runs
resolve the provider to this checkout's
`packages/anthropic/dist/index.js`; the captured resolution was:

```text
file:///Users/gr2m/.codex/worktrees/a91e/ai/packages/anthropic/dist/index.js
```

Before: both methods and both restricted choices sent `mcp_servers`
without `tool_configuration`, enabling connector tools by default.
`tool_choice` was `any`; ordinary tools were already filtered to `json`
for `none`, or `greeting` and `json` for the named choice.

Before the review correction: the four named-choice cases without a JSON
response format used `tool_choice: auto` and left MCP tools enabled on
Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 4.5 with manual thinking.

After: all eight requests send `tool_configuration: { enabled: false }`
for the connector. The internal JSON tool remains available, and the
named choice still includes only the selected application tool and JSON.

Verification limits: this is request construction and response parsing
against a synthetic provider transport, not live end-to-end
verification. No controlled live MCP connector was supplied; no real
Anthropic/MCP execution was attempted. Provider-side enforcement and
remote actions were not verified.

</details>

## Validation

- Before production changes, the new regression cases had 8 failures
(all restricted-choice cases) and 6 passes (all unrestricted-choice
cases).
- `pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/anthropic test`: 1,070 tests passed in Node and
1,070 passed in Edge.
- `pnpm check`: passed with zero warnings/errors.
- `pnpm type-check:full`: passed.
- Modified-file guideline discovery and verifiers: no applicable
guidelines/verifiers. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude Code Opus 5.5 review: completed using verified
`claude-opus-5-5`; fresh full-diff confirmation at `00371ee04b` found no
actionable findings and confirmed all three dispositions.
- Review finding 1 (named-choice fallback): confirmed by four failing
cases, fixed in signed commit `5d90e257e6`.
- Review finding 2 (preservation coverage): added eight cases in
separate signed commit `00371ee04b`.
- Review finding 3 (verification limits): disclosed above, with the
rationale for disabling connectors rather than removing their
descriptors.
- CI for `00371ee04b2724ef67efc7fefb12578775370cdb`: all 55 completed
checks passed, including all required checks and the CI/changeset
workflows. The external `Vercel Security Review` remains `IN_PROGRESS`
with summary `Reviewing deployments`, without findings or an error. It
has shown the same status for approximately 15 minutes. The PR remains
draft until that check completes successfully; no task-caused CI failure
was found.

fix(google-vertex): only send maas credentials to the maas api (#24692)

## background

the maas provider adds google cloud auth through a custom fetch, because
`createOpenAICompatible` only takes static headers. that fetch added
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` to every request, including image urls
from an image response and the hops of their redirects. `getFromApi`
already strips headers for those cross-origin downloads
(`credentialedOrigin`), but the wrapper put the token back, so a
response pointing at another host got a reusable google cloud token

## summary

- the node and edge wrappers only add the token and custom `headers`
when the request url has the same origin as the maas api, other requests
go through untouched and no token is generated for them
- move the base url logic into `loadGoogleVertexMaasBaseURL` so the
wrappers and the provider use the same url
- redirects are covered too, since each hop goes through the wrapper

## verification

before: an image url on another host (directly or after a redirect) got
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. after: only the maas api gets it

<details>
<summary>real provider + openai-compatible image model + download guard,
only the google token mocked</summary>

```
.../endpoints/openapi/images/generations -> Authorization: Bearer SECRET-GOOGLE-TOKEN

.../redirect-me -> Authorization: Bearer SECRET-GOOGLE-TOKEN
https://evil.example/after-redirect.png -> Authorization: Bearer SECRET-GOOGLE-TOKEN

after

fix(harness): enforce workDir / project-level config isolation where possible and clearly document the gap otherwise (#24626)

## Background

Repository-owned configuration can affect harness behavior, hooks, MCP
tools, and approvals. Harness adapters have different controls for
isolating that configuration, while project instructions and skills
still need deliberate handling.

Agent instructions and skills in the workDir are less sensitive because
the agent's execution isn't deterministic either way. But project-level
config that modifies the behavior of the harness itself should not be
automatically discovered and processed.

This was already fixed in #24415 for OpenCode. This PR handles it as far
as possible for the other harness adapters.

## Summary

- Add `repo-config-isolation` diagnostic examples for all `HarnessAgent`
adapters to exercise repository instructions, skills, hooks, write
approvals, and response behavior.
- Constrain project configuration loading where supported, while
maintaining support for project-level instructions and skills.
- Claude Code and Grok Build only support an all-in-one toggle, so they
now can no longer natively process project-level instructions and skills
in favor of a safer default.
- GitHub Copilot doesn't have a toggle at all, so its documentation now
covers that it must only be used with trusted workDir contents.

## Contributor Credit

N/A.

## End-to-End Verification

fix(harness-opencode): add `auth: 'direct'` to use native subscriptions when `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` is set (#24630)

## Background

With `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` set, the OpenCode adapter routes `xai`,
`github-copilot`, `poe`, `opencode-go` and `gitlab` through AI Gateway,
and no `auth` value lets their native subscriptions be used. `auth:
'openai'` and `auth: 'anthropic'` only cover those two providers, while
Claude Code, Codex and Cline already have `auth: 'direct'`. On Vercel
Sandbox this also happens when the user passes an OIDC token to
`@vercel/sandbox` but never sets the variable, because the Sandbox
client sets it after the first API call. Details and a Sandbox run are
in #24629.

## Summary

- Add `'direct'` to `OpenCodeAuthenticationMode`.
- With `auth: 'direct'`, `resolveOpenCodeEnv()` and
`resolveOpenCodeAuthenticationMode()` resolve the selected provider
(same default provider resolution as before) and skip the AI Gateway
check. Provider environment keys still win over a stored subscription.
- `auto`, `ai-gateway`, `anthropic`, `openai` and authentication records
behave as before.
- Document `direct` in the OpenCode adapter docs, including that
`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` counts as an AI Gateway credential under `auto`.
- Tests for `direct` with ambient `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and
`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` for each subscription provider, key precedence, the
default provider, a regression test that `auto` still uses AI Gateway
with an OIDC token, a harness-level Copilot test, and a type test.

## End-to-End Verification

I ran the offline `repro.mjs` from #24629 (full script there) against
the locally built `@ai-sdk/harness-opencode`, on `main` (`6737c772`) and
on this branch. It imports the package from the checkout's `dist`, calls
`createOpenCode().doStart()` with a fake `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, a fake
subscription per provider in a temporary `XDG_DATA_HOME` and a stub
sandbox session, and prints which credentials the adapter brokers for
each provider and `auth` value. It needs no credentials or network.

```sh
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/harness-opencode
node /outside/the/checkout/repro.mjs "$PWD/packages/harness-opencode/dist/index.js"
```

`auth: 'direct'` rows, before (`dist:
<checkout>/packages/harness-opencode/dist/index.js`, `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
set: true, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY set: false`):

```
openai          auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
xai             auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
github-copilot  auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
poe             auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
opencode-go     auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
gitlab          auth=direct     ai-gateway.vercel.sh <- VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
```

After (same header):

```
openai          auth=direct     chatgpt.com <- subscription
xai             auth=direct     api.x.ai <- subscription
github-copilot  auth=direct     api.githubcopilot.com <- subscription
poe             auth=direct     api.poe.com <- subscription
opencode-go     auth=direct     opencode.ai <- subscription
gitlab          auth=direct     cloud.gitlab.com <- subscription
```

All other rows are identical before and after: unset `auth` and `auth:
'ai-gateway'` still use AI Gateway with `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, `auth:
'openai'` still reaches the OpenAI subscription, and without the token
every provider resolves to its subscription in both runs.

Limits:

- I didn't send a model request with a real subscription after the fix.
The only non-OpenAI login I have is GitHub Copilot Free, and OpenAI was
already reachable with `auth: 'openai'`, so the script above is the
before/after evidence.
- I didn't repeat the Sandbox run from #24629 with this branch.
- The script stops before the bridge starts, so it shows which
credentials the host brokers and for which hosts, not how OpenCode uses
them.

commit.message:
fix(google): skip streamed tool-call array indexes that leave a gap (#24678)

## background

with `streamFunctionCallArguments`, vertex streams tool-call args as
`partialArgs` and the accumulator rebuilds them from json paths. array
indexes had no bound, so one small chunk like `$.items[20000000]` made a
sparse array and `finalize()` serialized every hole as `null`, turning a
50 byte chunk into a 100 MB tool input and blocking the process

real streams always send array elements in order starting at `[0]`

## summary

- an array index in a streamed path must be an existing element or the
next one, entries that would leave a gap are skipped like other invalid
paths
- this also keeps the streamed text deltas matching `finalize()`, they
disagreed before when an index skipped ahead
- tool input validation still catches anything required that gets
skipped

## verification

before: `$.items[20000000]` turned 50 bytes into a 100,000,013 char tool
input in ~500ms. after: it's skipped and the input stays `{}`

<details>
<summary>accumulator on main and release-v6.0</summary>

```
response chunk bytes: 50
main final JSON length: 100,000,013 ms: 519
v6 final JSON length: 100,000,013 ms: 493
```

</details>

- new tests for a huge first index, a gap and a nested gap (they check
the joined deltas equal `finalJSON`) plus a `doStream` test with a
sparse vertex stream, all fail without the fix
- the recorded vertex streams with nested array args still produce the
same input

fix(ai): hide transcription words from telemetry when recordOutputs is false (#24675)

## background

with `recordOutputs: false` telemetry hides the transcript `text` and
`segments` from `transcribe`, but `words` still goes through, so the
full transcript can be rebuilt from the word timings

## summary

- add `words` to the output fields `filterTelemetryEvent` clears when
`recordOutputs` is false
- the result returned to the caller still has the words

## verification

before: telemetry gets `text: ""` and no segments but all 85 words.
after: telemetry gets no words and the result still has all 85

<details>
<summary>live run with openai whisper-1</summary>

`transcribe` on `data/galileo.mp3` with `timestampGranularities:
['word', 'segment']` and an `onEnd` integration, `recordOutputs: false`

before

```
result words: 85 first: [{"text":"Galileo","startSecond":0,"endSecond":0.66},{"text":"was",...},{"text":"an",...}]
telemetry text: "" segments: 0 words: 85 [{"text":"Galileo","startSecond":0,"endSecond":0.66},{"text":"was",...},{"text":"an",...}]
```

after

```
result words: 85 first: [{"text":"Galileo","startSecond":0,"endSecond":0.66},{"text":"was",...},{"text":"an",...}]
telemetry text: "" segments: 0 words: 0 []
```

</details>
